item.description: Crèche and childcare in Basel-Stadt: crèches, day and after-school families, income-related tariffs and cantonal subsidies.
item.content:encoded:
## At a Glance - Daycare centers, family daycare, and after-school programs are the recommended options. - Childcare fees are calculated based on income. - Cantonal subsidies are available in the canton. - The Swiss tax system distinguishes between three levels: federal, cantonal, and municipal.
## Key Facts - Services → daycare centers, family daycare, and after-school programs - Fees → based on income - Support → cantonal subsidies available - Taxes → direct federal, cantonal, and municipal taxes
### Overview for Basel-Stadt
In the Canton of Basel-Stadt, child care is provided through three options: daycare centers, family daycare providers, and after-school programs. These are the categories families should compare when organizing child care and determining how to budget for it. For more details on the first option, see section asilo nido.
The economic criterion outlined is equally clear: rates are calculated based on income. The cost, therefore, must be considered in conjunction with the specific income situation. Before comparing services, it is advisable to identify the income used for the calculation and apply the same criterion to the alternatives under consideration.
In addition to the rates, the table lists available cantonal subsidies. This financial support should be evaluated alongside the chosen childcare solution and the income level used to determine the rate. The combination of service, income-based calculation, and subsidy forms the practical core of the information for those living in the canton.
This expense must be distinguished from taxes. The Swiss tax system includes direct federal tax, cantonal tax, and municipal tax. Each canton has its own law and its own multiplier; in municipalities, the multiplier applies to the cantonal tax.
Administrative responsibilities also follow this separation. The AFC/ESTV handles direct federal tax and VAT, while cantonal administrations manage cantonal and municipal matters. The UFAS/BSV is responsible for social security—including AVS, AI, and LPP—and does not set tax rates; The Federal Statistical Office (UST/BFS) produces statistics and does not set tax rates. Regarding child care, the correct interpretation depends on the Canton of Basel-Stadt, the type of service, and income, while taxes and social security remain separate categories. ## How to Interpret Expenses in the Family Budget
### Three Comparisons That Help Avoid Mistakes
The first comparison should be between services, not between figures taken from different contexts. A family evaluating daycare options can compare the costs of in-home daycare and after-school care, but must note which service each fee refers to. The source lists three types of childcare; the comparison must therefore keep them separate and apply the income criterion consistently.
The second comparison concerns income and cantonal subsidies. In a hypothetical scenario, the person preparing the budget can create one line item for the service, one for the income used in the calculation, and one for the subsidy to be verified. There’s no need for made-up amounts: what’s needed are the correct categories and the income figure applied to the chosen option. If the service changes, the comparison must be repeated.
The third comparison separates child care from other living expenses. LAMal/KVG is mandatory health insurance for residents, with per-capita premiums; it is neither a tax nor an employer contribution. Premiums depend on the canton or region, and premium reductions are a cantonal subsidy. In the budget, this item must be listed separately from child care support.
The same criterion applies to the pay stub. AVS/AHV and LPP/BVG are part of social security. Direct federal tax, VAT, and cantonal or municipal taxes, on the other hand, belong to the tax category. Cantons and municipalities play distinct roles in the tax system. To provide a more complete picture, include costo della vita in Svizzera alongside the specific child care calculation.
The practical result is a clear overview: services, income, subsidies, and other expenses remain easily identifiable. This prevents an insurance premium from being treated as a child care fee and ensures that tax or social security items are not mistakenly attributed to child care expenses.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## How to Move from Research to Decision-Making
### Four Practical Steps
1. Define the service. Start with your specific need and choose the option to explore: daycare, family daycare, or after-school care. List it separately so that each rate remains linked to the correct type of childcare. If your search concerns daycare, open section asilo nido along with the information from the Canton of Basel-Stadt.
2. Prepare the income data. Rates are calculated based on income. Before creating the comparison, identify the income required for the calculation and keep it separate from the fee. Avoid substituting the data with an average figure or another budget line item. To view the salary component, refer to busta paga svizzera.
3. Verify financial assistance. Cantonal subsidies are available for the specified childcare arrangement. Look up the guidelines from the Canton of Basel-Stadt regarding the chosen solution and verify the subsidy amount before including it in the budget. Record the fee and the subsidy separately: this distinction makes it clear which amount comes from the service and which from the subsidy.
4. Organize the budget by categories. Keep one section for childcare and another for other expenses. The tax category includes direct federal tax, cantonal tax, and municipal tax; the social security category includes AVS/AI/LPP; and the health category includes LAMal/KVG. This separation prevents you from attributing amounts that belong to taxes, premiums, or contributions to daycare centers, family daycare providers, or after-school programs.
When the family changes care arrangements, repeat the process without automatically carrying over the previous calculation: the item under review and the comparison to be made change, while income remains the central factor. If multiple forms of childcare are being evaluated, keep a separate record for each one. For the broader overview in costo della vita in Svizzera, list childcare expenses alongside the other items without mixing them up.
The budget remains clear if you use the correct service, apply the income-based criterion, verify the cantonal subsidy, and separate taxes, pension contributions, and health insurance. After organizing these items, complete the budget with the calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Cantonal Tax: A Comparison Between Switzerland in 2026 and Bern
item.description: In 2026, the tax comparison will be based on the federal direct tax, cantonal tax, and municipal tax; for Bern, the municipal multiplier will also be taken into account.
item.content:encoded:
## At a Glance - Taxation occurs at three levels: federal, cantonal, and municipal - Each canton applies its own laws and multiplier - The municipality applies a multiplier to the cantonal tax - AFC/ESTV administers direct federal tax and VAT
## Key Facts - Levels → direct federal tax, cantonal tax, and municipal tax - Cantons → their own laws and multipliers - Municipalities → a multiplier applied to the cantonal tax - AFC/ESTV → direct federal tax and VAT - LAMal/KVG → mandatory for residents
The Swiss tax system consists of three levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax, and municipal tax. When analyzing the 2026 comparison for the Canton of Bern, these three components must be considered separately, because each canton has its own law and multiplier, while municipalities apply a multiplier to the cantonal tax.
### Agencies and Responsibilities The AFC/ESTV oversees direct federal tax and VAT. Cantonal administrations, on the other hand, oversee the cantonal and municipal components. The result cannot be expressed as a single national percentage: the federal portion remains distinct from cantonal regulations and the municipal multiplier.
The Federal Social Insurance Office (UFAS/BSV) has a different role. It is responsible for social security, including AVS, AI, and LPP, but does not set tax rates. The Federal Statistical Office (UST/BFS) also plays a statistical role and does not establish tax rates. This distinction is intended to avoid confusion between those who administer tax collection and those who produce statistics or oversee social security.
| Entry | Reference | How to Interpret | | --- | --- | --- | | Direct Federal Tax and VAT | AFC/ESTV | Federal plan | | Cantonal and Municipal Taxes | Cantonal administrations | Cantonal law and municipal multiplier | | AVS/AI/LPP | UFAS/BSV | Social security, not a tax |
For those comparing Bern with other cantons, the practical sequence is therefore fixed: first, separate out the direct federal tax; then examine the cantonal portion; and finally, consider the municipal multiplier. The same framework must be maintained when using dichiarazione delle imposte; otherwise, there is a risk of comparing different components.
AVS/AI/IPG, AD/AC, LAINF/LAA, and LPP/BVG also belong to a separate category: payroll contributions. They are not the fourth tier of cantonal tax; they must be kept separate in the 2026 comparison. ## Items to keep separate
The calculation of the salary and the cantonal tax are not the same. Social security or insurance contributions may appear on the salary that follow different rules from the comparison between cantons.
### Contributions and awards For AHV/IV/EO, the employee's share is 5.3%; the total with the employer is 10.6%. AD/HC is worth 1.1% up to the annual ceiling. UVG/LAA ranges from 0.7% to 1.5% depending on the sector. For BVG/BVG, the percentages indicated on the coordinated salary are 7% between 25 and 34 years old, 10% between 35 and 44, 15% between 45 and 54 and 18% from 55 years old up to the reference age.
These items do not become cantonal tax rates just because they appear in the salary calculation itself. In the comparison on Bern, it is therefore clearer to keep a tax freeze and a contribution freeze, without automatically adding up quantities that have different functions.
The KVG follows yet another logic. For residents, it is a compulsory health insurance policy to be taken out within three months of arrival; it works with per capita premiums, not with a tax or wage contribution. Premiums vary by canton or region, and the premium reduction is cantonal. For adults, the available deductibles are CHF 300/500/1000/1500/2000/2500.
The cost of living should therefore not be read through the cantonal tax alone. The same caution is needed when comparing work: in Switzerland there is no federal minimum wage, although some cantons have their own. This is a figure to be kept separate from the tax grid.
Finally, legitimate optimisation strategies require up-to-date figures. The third pillar 3a ceiling, the BVG coordination threshold or deduction, the AD/AC ceiling, the average KVG premiums and the median salary are indexed figures each year. For a full reading, place the costo della vita in Svizzera next to the tax comparison and check the official source before using a 2026 amount.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## Practical Procedure for Bern
The 2026 comparison for the Canton of Bern becomes operational once each item is assigned to the correct level. A brief procedure prevents the use of a municipal multiplier as if it were a cantonal tax rate or the inclusion of LAMal premiums in the tax levy.
### Five Operational Steps 1. Identify the scope. Specify the Canton of Bern and the reference municipality. The canton should be interpreted according to its own law and multiplier; the municipality according to the multiplier applied to the cantonal tax.
2. Identify the responsible authorities. For direct federal tax and VAT, the reference is the AFC/ESTV. For the cantonal and municipal components, consult the cantonal administrations. The Federal Social Insurance Office (UFAS/BSV) and the Federal Statistical Office (UST/BFS) are not involved in tax determination: the former oversees social security, while the latter handles statistics.
3. Update the 2026 figures. Do not set amounts without verifying the 3a contribution limit, the LPP coordination threshold or deduction, the AD/AC limit, the average KVG premiums, and the median wage. These figures are indexed annually; use the updated official source.
4. Set the salary aside. Record AVS/AI/IPG, AD/AC, LAINF/LAA, and LPP/BVG separately. This prevents contributions and taxes from being added together and allows you to determine labor costs without converting contribution percentages into cantonal tax rates.
5. Check KVG requirements and planning. If you are a resident, health insurance is mandatory and must be obtained within three months of arrival. For adults, deductibles are CHF 300/500/1,000/1,500/2,000/2,500; premiums vary by canton or region, while premium reductions are determined at the cantonal level. For lawful optimization, apply only rules and figures verified for the specific canton and year in question.
To convert this table into a personalized estimate, use calcolatore stipendio/imposte.

item.title: Lake Zurich: Reduced Outflow Starting in October 2026
item.description: To combat the drought, starting October 1, 2026, the outflow from Lake Zurich will be reduced from 30 to 20 cubic meters per second to ensure safe navigation.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The runoff drops from 30 to 20 cubic meters per second - The measure starts on 1 October 2026 - FOEN and four cantons approved the cut - The reduction lasts, for now, until the end of October
## Key Facts - Decision → 30 September 2026 - Lake → Lake Zurich - Outflow → 30 to 20 cubic meters per second - Effective → 1 October 2026 - Duration → until the end of October - Coordination → the Canton of Zurich, the Cantons of Aargau, Schwyz and St. Gallen, FOEN - Effects considered → navigation, ferry, rescue, ecosystem and hydropower
On 30 September 2026, the Canton of Zurich, in agreement with the cantons of Aargau, Schwyz and St. Gallen and the FOEN, ordered the reduction of the runoff from Lake Zurich from 30 to 20 cubic metres per second. The measure will come into force on 1 October 2026 and will remain limited, for the time being, until the end of October.
The measure is intended to curb the lowering of the lake level and reduce the disruption to shipping, the Lake Zurich ferry and the rescue service. The operational downturn is an even lower flow into the Limmat, with consequences for the ecosystem and hydropower production.
### A drought-related decision
Upstream there is persistent drought: the water flowing into the lake is less than that flowing from it and the level continues to fall. According to current weather and runoff forecasts, no significant improvement is expected in the short term.
A further decline would be likely to jeopardise the ferry, the Zürichsee Schifffahrtsgesellschaft shipping company and the rescue service in particular. The construction site of the Rathausbrücke, organised by the City of Zurich, could also be affected: if the level was too low, it would no longer be possible to use the necessary floating pontoons. The work would therefore have to be stopped, with delays and additional costs.
In mid-July, in view of the impending heat wave, Zurich had already increased the runoff to 30 cubic metres per second. In August, in order to contain the risk of fish die-offs in the Limmat, the FOEN and the cantons involved confirmed the decision, although they took into account that the lake level could fall below the lower limit set by the Water Regulation Regulation.
Since then, the lake has fallen again. However, the temperatures in the Limmat have dropped and are no longer critical for psychrophilous species such as trout and grayling. At the request of Zurich, the FOEN and the cantons involved have therefore approved the new runoff level. The duration remains temporary: after the end of October, the situation will be reassessed, also in view of the upcoming trout spawning season. ## Why the reduction has opposite effects
The change from 30 to 20 cubic meters per second creates a balance between the lake and the Limmat. In the first case, it retains more water and slows the decline; in the second, it reduces the available flow. The press release therefore describes an operational benefit for the lake along with possible environmental and energy-related effects downstream.
### The Before-and-After Comparison
| Area | Before | With 20 cubic meters per second | |---|---|---| | Lake | level falling | slower decline | | Navigation | risk of disruptions | measures to mitigate them | | Limmat | higher flow rate | reduced depth and potential habitats | | Fish | more critical summer water conditions | lower risk of mass mortality, though effects cannot be ruled out | | Hydroelectric | production dependent on flow rate | reported consequences, without estimates |
The practical implications vary depending on the perspective. On the lake, a slightly higher water level should mitigate the difficulties indicated for ferries, navigation, and rescue operations. In the Limmat, however, reduced flow may decrease water depth and the number of habitats. The text does not translate these effects into a numerical forecast or an operational timeline.
The situation for fish remains twofold. The Zurich Cantonal Office for Fisheries and Game Management estimates a lower risk of fish mortality compared to the hot summer weeks, as temperatures are now less critical for trout and grayling. However, the lower flow rate may adversely affect other aquatic organisms, and negative consequences cannot be ruled out.
Regarding hydropower, the source mentions consequences but does not specify their nature or extent. It is therefore not possible to attribute a quantified reduction in production to the decision. Regarding the work on the Rathausbrücke, however, only the scenario of disruption, delays, and additional costs are mentioned if the pontoons cannot be used.
To distinguish this local effect from a measure affecting household budgets, the reader may consult costo della vita in Svizzera: the press release does not provide figures on household expenses. Regarding transportation, no new schedule has been announced; updates on mezzi pubblici remain separate from the hydrological measure.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to follow the measure until the re-evaluation
The press release does not indicate forms, requests or documents to be submitted. The practical procedure for the reader is therefore a verification of the dates and activities directly mentioned, without adding obligations that the source does not provide.
### Four operational steps
1. Effective date — mark 1 October 2026 as the start of the reduction. Until then, the new outflow is not indicated as having entered into force.
2. Navigation — if you have to use the Lake Zurich ferry or follow a navigation activity, check the operational communications of the service concerned: the measure was also created to contain possible inconvenience. The text does not communicate an alternative timetable.
3. Work on the bridge — those who follow the Rathausbrücke construction site must bear in mind the condition described: too low levels can prevent the use of floating pontoons, with possible interruption, delays and additional costs.
4. End of October — mark the end of October as the provisional deadline. The situation will be reassessed after the limited duration of the measure, also in view of the upcoming trout spawning period.
### The check to be done
The assessment does not only concern the level of Lake Zurich. The two effects indicated must be read together: more water retained in the lake on the one hand, lower flow into the Limmat on the other. For the latter, the source points to a possible reduction in depth and habitats, while the risk of die-off is now lower due to lower temperatures. The picture therefore remains open until the new assessment.
The press release does not quantify either the effects on hydroelectric production or the additional costs of the works. To accompany this verification with an estimate of household disposable income, use calcolatore stipendio.
*Source: [admin.ch](https://www.admin.ch/it/newnsb/AhGAmdNkdNPt)*

item.title: Working at SECO: Apprenticeships and Internships
item.description: SECO has more than 900 employees, three offices in Switzerland and around 30 secondments: apprenticeships, traineeships and translation mandates.
item.content:encoded:
## At a Glance - SECO has over 900 employees and executives. - Three offices in Switzerland and approximately 30 staff members stationed in various countries. - Offers AFC apprenticeships, SMC internships, and university internships.
## Key Facts - Workforce: over 900 employees and managers - Offices: three in Switzerland - Staff stationed abroad: approximately 30 in various countries - AFC apprenticeships: commerce, digital business, and information technology - Internships: SMC and university-level
Over 900 employees and managers work at SECO, spread across three locations in Switzerland. In addition to this workforce, there are approximately 30 staff members on assignment in various countries. The presentation thus describes an employer with an organized presence in Switzerland and a component that extends beyond national borders.
### Four Entry Pathways
The opportunities are not limited to a single profile. SECO offers AFC apprenticeships for commercial clerks, digital business developers, and IT professionals. Commercial high school interns are also welcome: the commercial high school internship is presented as a distinct path from the AFC apprenticeship.
For university students, the program offers a university internship. SECO presents this as a career starter in which interns can put their knowledge into practice, take on various responsibilities, and work on a range of concrete projects. The program is thus described in terms of operational activities and responsibilities.
SECO also highlights an area aimed at external collaborators. The language services provide various specialized services and have an extensive network of freelance translators who translate into the official languages or other languages.
In terms of the work environment, SECO emphasizes responsibility, open-mindedness, and personal initiative. The presentation is aimed at employees who wish to help shape Swiss economic policy and associates the work with purpose, responsibility, and excellent working conditions. SECO also states that it opens up new opportunities for those who want to contribute to Swiss economic policy. Training, apprenticeships, university internships, and language-related positions are therefore all part of the same career opportunity. For those considering a career path at SECO, a practical understanding begins with distinguishing between vocational training, apprenticeships, university internships, and external collaboration. These are not interchangeable terms: the source assigns a different function to each.
### The Career Path Map
| Path | Recommended Field or Profile | Described Element | |---|---|---| | AFC | Commercial clerks, digital business developers, and IT professionals | Apprenticeship | | SMC | Business school interns | Internship | | University | University interns | Applied knowledge, responsibility, and concrete projects | | Translation | External collaborators | Network of freelance translators in language services |
The AFC is the track to consider when your interest lies in commerce, digital business development, or the IT sector. The SMC internship, on the other hand, is designed for business school interns. This distinction clarifies the first step in the selection process: it’s not enough to simply look for a generic opportunity; you need to identify the pathway that aligns with your own career trajectory.
The university internship offers an additional dimension: it connects previously acquired knowledge with responsibility and concrete projects. Those evaluating the application can therefore view the proposal as a hands-on experience, not merely as time spent in the office. The description of the work environment adds three compatibility criteria: responsibility, open-mindedness, and personal initiative. These are the qualities that SECO states it values in its day-to-day work.
The translation track follows a different logic. It is aimed at external collaborators and is linked to the language services, which work with a broad network of freelance translators in the official languages or other languages. This distinction helps prevent confusion between an internal training opportunity and an external assignment.
The common thread highlighted in the presentation is the relationship between work and growth: SECO discusses new prospects for employees, while for university interns, it emphasizes the application of knowledge and projects. The choice can therefore be evaluated on two levels: the access channel and the specific content of the experience.
To broaden your search, you can consult the annunci di lavoro and aziende che assumono classifications. The point is not to compare different offers, but to use SECO’s classification to understand what type of experience to look for: an AFC apprenticeship, an SMC internship, a university internship, or a translation assignment.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. Anyone who wants to turn this description into a structured search can follow a checklist, without mixing up paths with different goals.
### Steps for Choosing
1. Define your starting point. The AFC apprenticeship covers the three fields listed: commercial clerks, digital business developers, and the IT sector. The SMC internship, on the other hand, is for business school interns. 2. If you’re a college student, distinguish your college internship from the other options. The key criteria to look for in the job description are the opportunity to apply your knowledge in practice, take on various responsibilities, and work on concrete projects. 3. If you work as a freelance translator, consider opportunities for freelance assignments. SECO’s language services have an extensive network and work in the official languages as well as other languages. 4. Compare your goals with the work environment described by SECO: responsibility, open-mindedness, and personal initiative are explicitly valued. 5. Keep the type of position distinct. An AFC apprenticeship, an SMC internship, a university internship, and a translation assignment are not presented as the same type of opportunity; recognizing the category helps you avoid searching for information using keywords that are too generic.
The sequence leads from the title of the opportunity to the nature of the experience. For an apprentice, the first filter is the AFC framework; for an SMC intern, the connection to the business school; for a university intern, the combination of knowledge, responsibility, and projects. For an external contractor, however, the reference is the language service and the freelance network.
A careful reading reduces the risk of attributing AFC characteristics to a university internship or of considering a freelance assignment as an internship. The terms used by SECO help keep the pathways separate and link each choice to the experience described. The same logic allows you to highlight what the presentation emphasizes: responsibility, open-mindedness, personal initiative, and the opportunity to work on concrete projects.
The search can then be supplemented with annunci di lavoro, while keeping the selected category as the selection criterion. To combine professional evaluation with a financial assessment, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Civil Protection: 9 days between Ticino and Como
item.description: Extramuro 2026 takes place from October 1 to 9: two days in Pollegio and five in the province of Como, featuring Italian and Swiss operators.
item.content:encoded:
## At a Glance - Extramuro 2026 takes place from October 1 to 9, 2026 - October 1–2: field exercise in Pollegio, Canton Ticino - October 5–9: activities in Erba, Merone, and Pusiano - Closing ceremony on October 9 at the CPE in Erba
## Key Facts - Program → “Extramuro 2026,” second edition - Dates → October 1–9, 2026 - Ticino phase → Pollegio, October 1 and 2 - Italian phase → Erba, Merone, and Pusiano, October 5–9 - Headquarters and closing → CPE in Erba, closing ceremony on October 9
From October 1 to 9, 2026, regions in Lombardy and Switzerland will host “Extramuro 2026,” the second edition of the joint training program dedicated to cross-border civil protection. Following its debut in 2024, the initiative aims to conduct field tests of the emergency response system for major emergencies between Italy and Switzerland.
### Two Phases in Ticino and the Province of Como
The program is divided between Switzerland and Italy and consists of two distinct phases. Activities on October 1 and 2 are concentrated in Pollegio, in the Canton of Ticino. From October 5 to 9, the focus of the exercise shifts to the province of Como, involving the municipalities of Erba, Merone, and Pusiano.
The training camp is located at the Erba Multipurpose Emergency Center, which also serves as the exercise headquarters. This location thus becomes the focal point for the phase taking place in the province of Como.
The portion of the exercise titled “Switzerland in Italy” is designed to train the Civil Protection Militia of the Canton of Ticino, following the reverse-scenario module conducted in June. The stated objective is to improve synergy and integration between emergency responders from the two countries in preparation for real emergencies.
Field operations are coordinated by the Lombardy Region’s General Directorate for Security and Civil Protection. The collaboration involves the Fire Department, AREU Lombardia, the Province of Como, and the Chiasso Police and Customs Cooperation Center.
During the activities, members of the public will see Italian and Swiss responders moving throughout the area in their respective vehicles and wearing their standard-issue uniforms. The event will officially conclude on Friday, October 9, with a closing ceremony at the CPE in Erba. The program thus combines an initial phase in Ticino with a second phase in the Como area, with a continued focus on joint emergency response training. ## Why the calendar is relevant for the Swiss public
For those who live or work in the Canton of Ticino, the most concrete element of the program is its presence in the cantonal territory and the possibility of distinguishing the two phases. On 1 and 2 October, the reference is Pollegio; from 5 to 9 October, the activity indicated by the source involves Erba, Merone and Pusiano, in the province of Como. The scan allows us to read Extramuro 2026 as an appointment distributed between Ticino and Lombardy.
### Two territories, one exercise
| Reading point | Useful data | |---|---| | Canton of Ticino | Pollegio hosts the activities of 1 and 2 October | | Province of Como | Erba, Merone and Pusiano are involved from 5 to 9 October | | Operations Center | The CPE in Erba hosts the school camp and the final ceremony |
Geography also helps to understand the operational significance of the initiative. The Ticino and Lombard parts are not presented as separate exercises: they are part of a joint training program between Italy and Switzerland. The declared goal is to improve synergy and integration between rescuers from the two states, so as to prepare collaboration in view of real emergencies.
For citizens, the visible consequence is precisely described: during the activities, Italian and Swiss operators move around the territory, with means and uniforms of ordinance. This information helps to correctly read what is seen in the areas concerned: the presence of the operators belongs to the exercise program.
The role of the CPE adds a stable reference to the phase in the province of Como. The center is the headquarters of the school camp and also hosts the closing ceremony. Those who have to organize travel on the indicated days can combine the calendar with information on mezzi pubblici, keeping the place of the first phase and the three municipalities of the second separate.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to Follow the Program
The source already provides the elements needed to create a practical sequence. The reader can use locations, dates, and the final ceremony as reference points, distinguishing between observing the exercise and its educational purpose.
### Daily Checklist
1. Mark the entire period from October 1 to 9, 2026, which includes the planned activities in both Switzerland and Lombardy.
2. Link October 1 and 2 to Pollegio, in the Canton of Ticino. This is the designated location for the first phase of the program.
3. Associate the period from October 5 to 9 with the municipalities of Erba, Merone, and Pusiano, in the province of Como. For travel planning, you may also consult the mezzi pubblici documents.
4. Use the Erba Multipurpose Emergency Center (CPE) as the base for the training camp and as the exercise headquarters.
5. Note the official closing on Friday, October 9: the closing ceremony will take place at the CPE in Erba. During the activities, the presence of Italian and Swiss responders, their respective vehicles, and standard-issue uniforms is part of the program.
This sequence allows you to associate each piece of information with a specific location and to track the transition from the Ticino phase to the phase in the province of Como. The objective remains as stated in the program: joint training and greater synergy among rescue personnel from both countries in preparation for real emergencies.
To fully navigate the site’s tools, also refer to calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Ticino, housing challenges discussed at Lugano’s LAC
item.description: HOMEspace, INFOpmi’s special event at the LAC, was presented: architecture, finance, and institutions came together to discuss the future of the Ticino region over the next 20 years.
item.content:encoded:
## At a Glance - HOMEspace presented at LAC Lugano Arte e Cultura - Roundtable discussion on Ticino over the next twenty years - The debate brought together architecture, finance, and institutions - Focus on quality, sustainability, and access to housing
## Key Facts - Event → Beyond Housing: Visions and Opportunities for an Increasingly Attractive Ticino - Location → LAC Lugano Arte e Cultura - Organizer → Grafica Set Group, with the support of the City of Lugano - Publication → HOMEspace, an INFOpmi special edition - Participants → Filippo Lombardi, Massimo Nicora, Marzio Grassi, Elena Guglielmin, David Dalsass, Riccardo Blumer, and Enrico Sassi
At LAC Lugano Arte e Cultura, Grafica Set Group presented HOMEspace, the new INFOpmi special issue dedicated to housing, architecture, and construction. The event, sponsored by the City of Lugano, focused on a specific question: Is Ticino ready to seize the opportunities and tackle the challenges of the next twenty years?
The starting point for the evening was the transformation of the relationship with the local area. Ticino—and, more broadly, Switzerland—have been described as magnets for individuals, families, and entrepreneurs seeking security and a better quality of life. Consequently, expectations regarding living spaces are also changing: luxury is no longer associated solely with ostentation and exclusivity, but with well-being, sustainability, services, healthy materials, technology, and harmony with the local environment.
Sacha Cattelan, CEO of Grafica Set Group SA, opened the proceedings by explaining the project’s editorial origins: > “It stems from a desire to offer a comprehensive exploration of the world of housing—a sector that plays a major economic role in Ticino and is closely linked to the region’s development and identity.”
He then linked the theme of the home to a broader question: not just how much to build, but how and what to build, and what kind of region to envision for the future.
### The Dialogue on Cities, Regulations, and Finance
Journalist and TV host Gianfranco De Santis moderated the discussion, which also included Enrico Sassi. Filippo Lombardi, head of the Department of Territorial Development for the City of Lugano, emphasized the need to strike a balance between residents, capital, urban identity, sustainability, regulations, appeals, and the relationship between the city center and the suburbs—with the goal of preventing housing from becoming a privilege reserved for the few.
Massimo Nicora addressed building regulations, exploring the tension between land protection and potential barriers to development, citing regulatory uncertainties, lengthy procedures, and the need for simplification. Marzio Grassi, Regional Head of Corporate & Real Estate for Ticino at UBS, offered the perspective of international capital, asset security, and risk assessment for modern and traditional properties through the lens of sustainability criteria. Elena Guglielmin, Senior Credit Analyst at UBS, discussed residential lending standards, the gap between supply and demand for future-proof properties, and young people’s access to mortgage loans.
David Dalsass spoke about the demand for quality, the value of a project for the neighborhood, and the relationship between regulation and large-scale developments. The design segment was opened by architect and designer Riccardo Blumer. The practical issue that emerged in Lugano concerns the very definition of “living.” The discussion does not treat it as a simple sum of square meters: it brings together the quality of the property, urban identity, sustainability, financing, and the ability to carry out projects. For those who live or work in Switzerland, this perspective shifts the focus from merely having a home to the conditions that make a project consistent with the local context.
### Quality and Access Are Not the Same Thing
The source uses the term “luxury” in a sense distinct from ostentation. Well-being, amenities, healthy materials, technology, and harmony with the local area become indicators of quality. The term “future-proof” appears in the comparison between supply and demand for quality real estate. Sustainability also plays a role in risk assessment for both modern and traditional properties. A project is thus evaluated based on the features it offers and the relationship it builds with the local area, not merely on its exclusivity.
The second key issue is access. Lombardi highlighted the relationship between the city center and the suburbs and the need to ensure that housing does not become a privilege for the few. Guglielmin added the issue of access to mortgage credit for younger people. For a family or a new resident, the assessment thus concerns both the quality of the housing supply and the standards required by the banking sector.
The third issue concerns timelines and regulations. Nicora described building bureaucracy as a balance between protection and a potential obstacle to development. Regulatory uncertainties and lengthy procedures can discourage investors; Lombardi also highlighted the burden of regulations and appeals in the planning process. Dalsass linked regulation to the ability to carry out large-scale projects.
The fourth factor is financial. Grassi pointed to financial security and projects with high added value as elements sought after by international capital. Dalsass refocused attention on the value a project generates for the entire neighborhood. This is not an administrative procedure: it is a framework for analyzing and distinguishing between quality, the local area, regulations, and financing.
### Five Steps to Evaluate a Project
1. Define the desired quality. Prioritize well-being, amenities, healthy materials, technology, sustainability, and harmony with the local area. These are the elements associated with the new concept of luxury and help describe what you’re looking for, without limiting yourself to exclusivity.
2. Examine the relationship with the neighborhood. Assess how the project fits into the city center or the suburbs and what value it can generate for the entire neighborhood. The question concerns not only the residential unit itself but also the local area that hosts it.

item.title: Parental leave in Switzerland: duration and IPG allowance
item.description: In Switzerland, maternity leave lasts 14 weeks with an 80% IPG benefit; paternity leave lasts 2 weeks.
item.content:encoded:
## At a Glance - Maternity: 14 weeks at 80% (IPG) - Paternity: 2 weeks - AVS/AI/IPG: 5.3% paid by the employee
## Key Facts - Maternity → 14 weeks at 80% (IPG) - Paternity → 2 weeks - AVS/AI/IPG → 5.3% paid by the employee, 10.6% total - AD/AC → 1.1% up to the annual cap
### The National Framework
Fourteen weeks of maternity leave with an 80% IPG benefit and two weeks of paternity leave are the two key figures to consider when examining parental leave in Switzerland. The duration is expressed in weeks; the explicit financial benchmark is 80% for maternity leave. For paternity leave, the available figure is a duration of two weeks.
For the daily allowance, the key figure to note is therefore the 80% rate associated with maternity leave. For paternity leave, the figure to use is the two-week duration; 80% remains the rate specified for maternity leave. A proper comparison must be based on this distinction, not on a single figure applied to both parents.
The initial analysis can be summarized in a simple table:
| Leave | Specified Duration | |---|---| | Maternity | 14 weeks | | Paternity | 2 weeks |
The term IPG accompanies the maternity data and identifies the allowance reference. It should not be confused with other wage-based contribution items. AVS/AI/IPG, AD/AC, LAINF/LAA, and LPP/BVG are, in fact, presented as wage-based contributions, with different rates and criteria. For a more detailed overview, refer to guida al congedo parentale.
Allowances require separate consideration. The cantonal context is part of the practical challenge: families should not take the leave data and assume it automatically represents the amount of an allowance. The duration of the absence and the associated financial support are items that must be checked separately, especially when the comparison involves multiple cantons.
Within the Swiss framework, the procedure is straightforward: determine whether it is maternity or paternity leave, note the corresponding duration, and use the 80% IPG as the standard benchmark for maternity leave. Other details should be based on the salary and the relevant canton, without converting a duration figure into a cantonal amount. ## How to Interpret the Economic Impact
### Separating Allowances and Wage Components
The 80% figure should be distinguished from the percentages of payroll contributions. For social security, the AVS/AI/IPG figure, which corresponds to the AVS/AHV line item, is 5.3% for the employee and 10.6% in total when combined with the employer’s contribution. AD/AC is 1.1% up to the annual cap, while LAINF/LAA ranges from 0.7% to 1.5% depending on the sector. The LPP/BVG, based on the coordinated salary, follows the following rates: 7% for those aged 25 to 34, 10% for those aged 35 to 44, 15% for those aged 45 to 54, and 18% from age 55 up to the reference age.
| Contribution Category | Data | |---|---| | AVS/AI/IPG | 5.3% employee; 10.6% total including employer | | AD/AC | 1.1% up to the annual cap | | LAINF/LAA | 0.7–1.5% depending on sector | | LPP/BVG | 7% (25–34), 10% (35–44), 15% (45–54), 18% (55+ up to the reference age) |
The first comparison to make is between the benefit and the salary: the IPG percentage is not a figure to be mechanically added to the other rates. The LPP/BVG, for example, is linked to the coordinated salary and age brackets; the AD/AC is also linked to the annual cap. A single percentage cannot therefore represent all items on the pay stub.
This separation is also important for household budgeting. LAMal/KVG coverage is mandatory for residents and must be obtained within 3 months of arrival. Premiums are per capita: they are neither a tax nor a payroll contribution. They vary by canton and region, while the premium reduction is a cantonal subsidy. In a family’s cost of living calculations, therefore, LAMal should be listed in a separate column from the IPG allowance. To navigate these items, the guide to cassa malati LAMal is available.
The minimum wage also does not provide a single federal standard: there is no federal minimum wage, and some cantons have their own. This information ensures that the parental leave parameter is not replaced by a local wage threshold. Cantonal allowances, for their part, should be treated as a separate item: the parental leave data remains distinct from the verification process conducted by the relevant canton for the allowance.
For practical purposes, it is advisable to open the busta paga svizzera file and place the IPG reference alongside it, without automatically adding together contributions, LAMal premiums, and allowances. The result is a clearer picture of the budget: duration on one side, economic parameters on the other, and the cantonal component separated.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## Practical Application Procedure
### Five Checks Before Submitting the Application
The preparation process can be broken down into five checks. The goal is to prevent a duration, a rate, and a benefit from being assigned to the same entry.
- 1. Identify the type of leave. Select “maternity” or “paternity”: the form uses two different durations—14 weeks for maternity and 2 weeks for paternity. - 2. Set the correct financial parameter. For maternity leave, enter 80% IPG. For paternity leave, enter the 2-week duration and do not automatically transfer the percentage used for maternity leave. - 3. Review the payroll line items. On the pay stub, separate AVS/AI/IPG, AD/AC, LAINF/LAA, and LPP/BVG; the percentages are not interchangeable, and some depend on the sector, age, or annual cap. - 4. Separate the allowances. Indicate the relevant canton and keep the cantonal entry separate from the IPG parameter. Do not use the duration of leave as the allowance amount. - 5. Complete the family budget. Exclude LAMal/KVG from the salary contribution: for residents, it is mandatory, with per-capita premiums, and enrollment must occur within 3 months of arrival. For the cost-of-living portion, you can use guida al costo della vita in Svizzera.
This sequence makes the request verifiable even when comparing situations across different cantons. First, define the event; then set the duration; and finally, check the IPG parameter and the compensation items. Allowances remain at the cantonal level; LAMal remains at the per-capita premium level. Keeping these lines separate prevents the leave-related payment from being interpreted as a new wage contribution or a tax.
For the final check, the key information to include in your file is a summary sheet: type of leave, duration, specified economic parameter, and canton where the benefits are paid. In the case of maternity leave, the 80% IPG rate is the figure to report; in the case of paternity leave, the entry to record is the two-week duration. The rest is verified based on the salary and the cantonal regulations, without adding amounts not listed in the table.

item.title: Coop reaches 1'000 supermarkets in Switzerland
item.description: Tomorrow, Coop’s 1,000th store will open in Emmen: 2,500 m². CEO Philipp Wyss announces new store openings and highlights the group’s leadership position in Ticino.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Coop will open its thousandth supermarket in Emmen tomorrow - The new store measures 2'500 square meters - The network covers about 1,1 million square meters - In Ticino, Coop describes itself as the market leader
## Key facts - Milestone → 1'000 supermarkets - Opening → tomorrow - Location → Emmen, canton of Lucerne - Area → 2'500 square meters - Investments over ten years → about 3,5 billion francs
Tomorrow, in Emmen in the canton of Lucerne, Coop will open the thousandth store in its supermarket network. The new store will have an area of 2'500 square meters and will bring the cooperative to the milestone of 1'000 supermarkets in Switzerland.
### An expansion measured in stores and floor space The milestone comes after ten years during which Coop opened 124 new branches and invested about 3,5 billion francs in renovating its stores. Overall, the stores occupy about 1,1 million square meters of retail space. The figure therefore combines new openings and work on existing stores.
The network is spread across very different settings. It starts in city centers, passes through villages and reaches mountain locations. Coop cites Bettmeralp, in Valais, at an altitude of 1'948 meters, as an example of its presence at high altitude. This example shows that the network includes urban locations, small centers and Alpine destinations.
### The next chapter of growth For CEO Philipp Wyss, the thousandth store does not mark the end of the group's growth. In his assessment, the potential remains mainly in Central and Eastern Switzerland, as well as in Geneva and Lausanne. Wyss also described Coop's position in some of Switzerland's main cities:
> «In Zurich and Basel we are extremely strong, and in Ticino we are the market leader».
After reaching the Emmen milestone, the group will continue opening new stores, the CEO announced. The announcement therefore links tomorrow's opening to the intention to continue opening stores in the locations indicated by Wyss. Coop is also focusing on integrating traditional and online retail, with the option of ordering groceries on Coop.ch and having them delivered to a store in their holiday destination. ## A Comparison with Migros The size of the chain becomes clearer when considering both the number of stores and the retail space. At the end of 2025, Migros had 659 standalone supermarkets, with just under 1.06 million square meters of retail space. Coop now has 1,000 supermarkets and approximately 1.1 million square meters.
### Two Network Strategies | Operator | Network and Retail Space | Upcoming Openings | |---|---|---| | Coop | 1,000 supermarkets; approximately 1.1 million m² | Announced new openings | | Migros | 659 standalone supermarkets as of the end of 2025; just under 1.06 million m² | 140 by 2030 |
This comparison features two operators with extensive networks and already announced expansion plans. For Migros, the timeline is specific: 140 new openings planned by 2030. For Coop, however, CEO Philipp Wyss has announced that expansion will continue beyond the 1,000th store.
For those living in Switzerland, the key takeaway also concerns geographic distribution. Coop mentions city centers, villages, and mountain towns, while pointing to additional potential in central and eastern Switzerland, as well as in Geneva and Lausanne. The network is therefore not described as concentrated in a single city, but rather as a presence spread across different types of locations.
### What to Watch for in the Next Moves The practical distinction lies between the store opening tomorrow in Emmen, the location announced in Ticino, and the areas where management sees further potential. These are three distinct pieces of information: a new opening, a market positioning, and a strategic direction for future openings. Readers can thus distinguish between the information already announced and the outlook outlined by the CEO.
The comparison with Migros also has a temporal dimension: Coop reports reaching its 1,000th supermarket, while Migros is aiming for 140 openings by 2030. To connect this dynamic to household expense management, readers can consult costo della vita in Svizzera.

item.title: Scuol closes schools in Ftan and Tarasp, parents appeal
item.description: The Scuol municipal government plans to close two schools by 2028/29 for financial and demographic reasons. Parents have filed an appeal with the Graubünden Court of Appeals.
item.content:encoded:
## At a Glance - Closure of Ftan and Tarasp by the 2028–2029 school year - Children from Ftan would attend school in Ardez - Children from Tarasp would attend school in Sent - Parents’ appeal to the Graubünden Court of Appeals
## Key Facts - Municipality → Scuol - School locations → five - Population → approximately 4,600 residents - Reasons cited → financial and demographic - Appeal → group of parents - Deadline for the municipality → October 20 - Merger agreement → signed in 2014 - Validity period stated by Riet Fanzun → through the end of 2029
### The Decision Announced in Scuol
In mid-September, during an informational meeting, the Scuol Municipal Council announced its intention to close the school campuses in Ftan and Tarasp by the 2028–2029 school year. The decision affects two of the five schools in the municipality—which is the largest in Switzerland by area—and, according to the municipal council, is based on financial and demographic reasons.
In the future, children from Ftan would attend school in Ardez, while those from Tarasp would be sent to Sent. Scuol has a population of approximately 4,600.
The announcement has sparked confusion among residents. This frustration led to an appeal: a group of parents filed it with the Graubünden Court of Appeals, which confirmed the news first reported by the Südostschweiz.
Mayor Aita Zanetti, a member of the Center Party, acknowledged that the reorganization—especially in Ftan and Tarasp—would fuel opposition and a heated, emotionally charged debate. The municipal council has taken note of the appeal and stated that it respects this process.
Over the past two weeks, the municipal executive has received letters from students and two petitions: one from Ftan and one from Tarasp. Zanetti said that the concerns and requests are being taken seriously. The municipal council also proposed a meeting with the students, but so far the invitation has not been accepted.
The campaign’s coordinating committee has received support from the Anna Florin Association, which has been working for years to preserve affordable housing and keep small villages in the canton of Graubünden alive. Riet Fanzun, a member of the steering committee and a resident of Tarasp, argues that schools help keep outlying villages attractive.
> “We know from studies that once a school is closed, there’s no going back.”
Meanwhile, the municipal government is continuing its work on the future organization of the school system. Following the appeal, the municipality will have until October 20 to respond. ## The Issue: Costs and Local Presence
### Comparing Two Criteria
The reorganization creates tension between two criteria that the text presents separately. On the one hand, City Hall wants to plan the school system for the coming years by considering the entire municipality and financial sustainability. On the other hand, parents supported by the Anna Florin Association link decentralized school locations to the appeal of outlying villages. The school itself is thus viewed both as a service to be organized and as a local institution.
| Profile | Key points in the case | |---|---| | School network | The municipality has five school locations; Ftan and Tarasp are the ones affected by the closure plan. | | Destinations | Children from Ftan would go to Ardez; those from Tarasp to Sent. | | City Hall’s Rationale | The decision is motivated by financial and demographic factors. | | Parents’ Objection | According to Riet Fanzun, the closure would make outlying villages less attractive. |
On a practical level, the transition from a local school to another municipal school changes the educational reference point for children and parents. The text lists the destination locations but does not specify distances, schedules, organized transportation, or expected savings. For this reason, the plan cannot be translated into a precise calculation of the cost or time required for commuting. For a general overview of the mezzi pubblici initiative, this issue must be kept separate from the decisions still under discussion in Scuol.
The timeline is also fueling the controversy. The closure is scheduled to take place by the end of the 2028–2029 school year, while Riet Fanzun argues that the municipal merger agreement, signed in 2014, requires that the campuses be maintained in a decentralized manner until the end of 2029. His argument does not concern only the appropriateness of the reorganization; it concerns who has the authority to decide and with what level of consent.
According to Fanzun, in the ten years following the agreement’s signing, the public should have the opportunity to vote on any changes, and the decision would require a two-thirds majority. The appeal thus brings a matter that is at once educational, territorial, and procedural before the Graubünden Court of Appeals. The City Council’s position remains different: the executive branch considers it necessary to have a reliable, pedagogically sound, and financially sustainable school system. For a separate breakdown of daily expenses, please refer to costo della vita in Svizzera.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## Steps to Follow
### The Documented Sequence
To follow the case without confusing announcements, appeals, and local participation, the steps already outlined can be organized as follows:
1. Mark the October 20 deadline. Following the appeal filed by the parents, the municipality has until that date to respond. This is the next explicit deadline communicated in this matter.
2. Distinguish between the administrative and judicial processes. The closure of Ftan and Tarasp is the municipality’s plan; the appeal to the Graubünden Court of Appeal is the parents’ initiative. The text does not yet indicate the outcome of the proceedings.
3. Verify the reference to the 2014 contract. Riet Fanzun cites the clause that would maintain the schools in a decentralized manner until the end of 2029. According to his interpretation, any changes would require a public vote and a two-thirds majority.
4. Keep the channels of participation that have already emerged distinct from one another. The letters from the students and the two petitions—one from Ftan and one from Tarasp—represent the initiatives mentioned following the announcement. The meeting proposed by the municipal government to the students has not yet been accepted.
5. Monitor the work on the future organization. The municipal government states that it intends to assess the coming years and the entire municipality, with the goal of ensuring a reliable, pedagogically sound, and financially sustainable school system.
This sequence allows for a separate analysis of the procedural deadline, the interpretation of the contract, and the public’s initiatives. It also avoids presenting a closure as definitive when, in the source, it is described as the Town Hall’s plan, while the appeal remains at the center of the matter.
For those following the case, the most immediate action point is therefore the municipality’s response by October 20. To combine this analysis with a review of your own budget, use calcolatore stipendio e imposte.

item.title: 2027 Budget: A Deficit of 98.5 Million and Controversy
item.description: The State Council presents a budget with a deficit of 98.5 million. The Greens criticize the measure, calling it electoral and lacking investment.
item.content:encoded:
## At a Glance - The 2027 budget projects a deficit of 98.5 million. - The Greens call it an “election budget.” - Cuts are proposed for services, staff, asylum, vulnerable individuals, and municipalities. - Balancing the budget has been postponed to the 2028–2030 period.
## Key Facts - Location → Bellinzona - Date → September 30, 2026 - Proposer → State Council - Operating deficit → 98.5 million francs - Criticism → Greens of Ticino - Financial plan → day-to-day management 2028–2030
On September 30, 2026, in Bellinzona, the 2027 budget presented by the State Council was described by the Greens of Ticino as an “election budget.” The proposal projects an operating deficit of 98.5 million francs. This assessment was communicated that evening in a statement signed by Samantha Bourgoin, the party’s co-coordinator.
According to the environmentalist party, the document relies primarily on spending cuts and does not provide sufficient investments to address future challenges. The statement also criticizes the fact that no tax increases are planned, not even for those who could afford the burden. Instead of addressing revenue, the budget focuses on spending cuts that, according to the Greens, affect services, staff, asylum, vulnerable individuals, and municipalities one by one.
In terms of investments, the party points out the absence of measures aimed at helping citizens and businesses face two explicitly identified challenges: the climate crisis and the aging population.
### The Postponed Shift
The Greens cite studies comparing Ticino’s spending with that of other cantons. In their view, these comparisons have revealed the limitations of the approach attributed to the majority parties—summarized in the refrain of tax breaks for the wealthy and cuts to wasteful government spending. Unilateral solutions, they argue, are not enough. The statement adds that the State Council had already begun last year—albeit tentatively—to take action on the revenue side as well.
The shift in course has been postponed until the start of the next legislative term. The government plans a package to rebalance the 2028–2030 Financial Plan for current operations. It will need to address spending through additional structural measures and sectoral reforms, consider revenue sources, and explore possible adjustments to financial relations with the Confederation and the municipalities. The Greens say that, for now, they will analyze the budget in detail, seeking to invest in the future and protect the most vulnerable people, given the Grand Council’s limited room for maneuver. To follow the fiscal chapter without attributing unannounced measures to the budget, readers can start with the guide to dichiarazione delle imposte. When reviewing the budget, it is important to distinguish between the short term and the reforms promised for the future. The 2027 plan is criticized as a temporary measure; the shift in policy is postponed until the start of the next legislative term; the announced package concerns day-to-day management for 2028–2030. This sequence shifts the focus from annual figures to decisions on fiscal rebalancing.
### Four Key Areas to Monitor
| Area | Key Aspects to Monitor | |---|---| | Expenditures | Structural measures and sectoral reforms | | Revenues | Reflection on taxation | | Financial Relations | Possible measures involving the Confederation and municipalities | | Investments | Identified challenges: climate crisis and aging |
For those living in Ticino, the most concrete point is the list of sectors that the Greens say will be affected: services, personnel, asylum, vulnerable individuals, and municipalities. The source does not assign a separate amount to each item. It is therefore not possible to convert the overall deficit into a figure per household, business, or municipality without adding data that is missing from the note.
The report takes two directions. The government outlines spending, reforms, and financial reports; the Greens call for a review of the tax system and deem unilateral solutions insufficient. The debate thus pits spending cuts against the search for new revenue, while investments in climate action and aging remain an unquantified political demand.
The absence of a tax increase in 2027 does not, according to the source’s analysis, mean that the revenue issue has been resolved: that topic is included in the chapters of the next phase. This distinction is also useful to avoid confusing the canton’s budget with the costo della vita in Svizzera, which follows a different framework.
The Greens consider it difficult, in the short term, to change financial flows with the municipalities—following the total failure of Ticino 2020—or with the Confederation, because a revision of fiscal equalization is not imminent. For the purposes of this analysis, these channels must be kept separate from internal spending measures.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. The operational part involves following the path outlined by the source, without jumping ahead to decisions that the text addresses later on. A resident, a business, or a municipality can create a monitoring report in five steps.
### Five Operational Steps
1. Set the 2027 target. Record the budget as an annual report and separate the expense items listed in the note: services, personnel, childcare, vulnerable individuals, and municipalities.
2. Note what is not planned. The Greens’ note states that no tax increases are planned, not even for those who could bear the burden. Therefore, do not include any tax changes in this phase other than those indicated.
3. Isolate the investment section. In the political debate, verify whether the proposals address support for citizens and businesses in light of the climate crisis and the aging population.
4. Follow the parliamentary process. A useful point of reference is the leeway granted to the Grand Council, which the Greens consider insufficient; take note of the positions that emerge from the analysis of the budget.
5. Set the schedule for the next phase. At the start of the next legislative term, review the 2028–2030 budget package across the four areas indicated: spending, sectoral reforms, revenue, and financial relations with the Confederation and municipalities.
### How to Avoid Premature Interpretations
This sequence helps keep measures potentially under discussion for 2027 separate from the structural measures announced for the 2028–2030 budget period. It also avoids turning the overall deficit into an individual cost: the document lists areas and guidelines but does not assign a specific figure to each service, person, or municipality. On the fiscal front, a discussion of revenue remains distinct from the absence of tax increases envisaged in the budget outlined by the Greens.
To translate the debate on revenue into a personal assessment, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Swisscom Layoff After 38 Years: The Case Goes to Bern
item.description: Sébastien Perriard, a 54-year-old from Bulle, was fired by Swisscom after 38 years of service. More than 530 people have signed a petition calling for his reinstatement.
item.content:encoded:
## At a Glance - Sébastien Perriard was fired by Swisscom after 38 years - The online petition has garnered over 530 signatures - Benoît Gaillard brought the case to the Federal Council
## Key Facts - Person → Sébastien Perriard - Location → Bulle - Company → Swisscom - Tenure → 38 years - Support → over 530 petition signatures
## A Dismissal That Has Reached the Federal Level
In Bulle, Sébastien Perriard’s story has moved from a personal matter to a public debate. The 54-year-old from Fribourg was fired by Swisscom after 38 years for helping an elderly customer who wanted to cancel some subscriptions. According to the account provided by the source, the employee had been reported by the store manager.
After the story became public, Perriard received an outpouring of solidarity—not just from customers. An online petition calls for him to be reinstated to his former position. At the time of this report, more than 530 people had signed it. The petition expresses outrage over what it calls a brutal dismissal and also calls for a review of sales practices at Swisscom stores to protect the most vulnerable customers.
### Solidarity from Former Colleagues
Among the comments on the petition is one from another former Swisscom employee. The former colleague recalled his excellent relationship with Perriard and explained that he struggled to understand the reasons for his dismissal. He described Perriard as collaborative and attentive, noting that this was consistent with his character—for instance, he had accompanied a neighbor to the Bulle store to clarify a situation that was deemed unclear.
The 54-year-old said he was also moved by the support of people who do not know him personally. He explained that this solidarity gives him strength.
> “It makes me feel less alone. I sincerely thank everyone.”
The message from his former colleague touched him particularly deeply, as it came after years without contact.
The case has also reached the federal level. Vaud National Councilor Benoît Gaillard raised the issue during question time in the Federal Council, asking whether a dismissal after nearly 40 years, without any warning, was compatible with modern and socially responsible personnel policies. In its response, the government remained cautious because it was not familiar with the specific case.
Gaillard then explained the nature of his efforts to the residents of the Fribourg town. He intends to submit a parliamentary question to inquire whether there is a problem with Swisscom and criticized the Federal Council’s response, claiming that he had already heard reports of unlawful practices at the company. ## What changes, and what does not change, for the labour market
The case does not, on its own, introduce a new rule for people working in Switzerland. The source does not report a judicial decision, a reinstatement agreement or a change already approved in sales procedures. Perriard's dismissal, the customers' petition and the parliamentary initiative announced by Gaillard therefore remain distinct.
### Three levels not to conflate
| Level | Information available | Undefined point | |---|---|---| | Individual employment relationship | Dismissal after 38 years and assistance to an elderly customer | Outcome of the matter | | Customers and sales | More than 530 signatures and request for reinstatement | Outcome of the petition | | Federal politics | Question to the Federal Council and announced interpellation | Outcome of the initiative |
The first practical implication concerns the difference between public solidarity and a company's decision. The more than 530 signatures show the support gathered by Perriard, but the source does not say that Swisscom has changed its decision. The petition should therefore be presented as a request, not as reinstatement already obtained.
The second concerns the protection of vulnerable customers. The request to review sales methods in stores does not describe a new procedure and does not establish widespread conduct. It is an issue raised by the signatories, linked to the incident at the Bulle store. The petition's text thus broadens the discussion: not only the fate of an employee, but also the way some customers' needs are handled.
The third implication is political. A member of the National Council brought the case up during Question Time and announced an interpellation. The government's cautious response nevertheless indicates that, based on the information available, no federal assessment of the specific case has been provided.
For those seeking a separate overview of professional opportunities in Switzerland, the case is not enough to describe the entire labour market. The search should be kept separate from the matter and can start from aziende che assumono, without attributing consequences to Swisscom that the source does not report.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to Follow Developments Without Adding Unverified Facts
The source provides a concrete timeline for following the case but does not offer a complete legal account. It does not specify the date of the dismissal, the text of any agreement, an official statement from Swisscom, or the outcome of subsequent actions. Those seeking information should therefore focus on the steps that are actually documented.
### Four Practical Steps
1. Separate facts from commentary. The verifiable core of the story includes Sébastien Perriard’s name, his 38-year career, the store in Bulle, his assistance to an elderly customer in canceling certain subscriptions, and the store manager’s report.
2. Distinguish the petition’s demands. The text calls for Perriard’s reinstatement to his former position and a review of sales practices in Swisscom stores, with a focus on the most vulnerable customers. The more than 530 signatures reflect the level of support gathered but do not guarantee that the demands will be met.
3. Follow the political process. Gaillard has already raised the issue during question time in the Federal Council and announced his intention to submit a parliamentary inquiry. The source does not specify a deadline, a date for submission, or a subsequent response: these details should not be anticipated.
4. Do not turn an individual case into a general rule. The account does not establish that every dismissal after many years will spark the same debate, nor does it convey a decision applicable to all Swisscom employees.
This approach also helps those working or seeking work in Switzerland to distinguish an individual case from broader assessments of personnel policies. For a separate search for career opportunities, you can consult the annunci di lavoro listings, without presenting them as a consequence of the Perriard case.
Finally, anyone wishing to compare their own compensation situation can use the calcolatore stipendio.

A reader can therefore start with the name of the subscription they are evaluating, note the category to which it belongs, and then move on to the pricing details and benefits listed in the available documentation.
